Sioux Falls property tax is billed by the offices named below.

Who bills what in Sioux Falls

  • Minnehaha County Director of Equalization handles assessment.
  • Minnehaha County Treasurer bills and collects the tax.

Due dates

Half due by April 30 and half by October 31 (statewide schedule; the Minnehaha Treasurer pages opened did not state dates). Not delinquent if half paid before May 1 and the remainder before Nov 1.. See the official page.

Challenging your assessment

Per the SD DOR 2026 appeal guide: assessment notices mailed by March 1; written appeal to the clerk of the local board of equalization by March 12 (2026 dates); local board meets March 16-20 and must give written decision by March 27; then written appeal to the county auditor by April 7 for the county board of equalization (meets April 14-May 5; decision notice by May 8); then Office of Hearing Examiners by May 15 or circuit court within 30 days of notice. Dates are the 2026 cycle; verify for th. See the official page.

Tax rate

We could not confirm the current Sioux Falls rate on an opened page, so we do not state one.

Local notes

  • Census Vintage 2025 population 213748; spans Minnehaha County (172103) and Lincoln County (41645) per SUMLEV 157.
  • Minnehaha DOE page states the office provides for review and appeal of assessments; appeal-process page (opened) gave no dates.

Sioux Falls by the numbers

With about 197,642 residents, Sioux Falls is number 1 of the 3 South Dakota places in this guide by population (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). Census respondents put the median owner-occupied home in Sioux Falls at $271,400, 12% below the South Dakota median for these places. Renters live in about 40% of Sioux Falls homes, and owners in 60%, where the South Dakota median is 63% owners. A median build year of 1992 puts the typical Sioux Falls house near 31 years old. These numbers describe Sioux Falls as a whole, so a given street can sit well above or below them.
